Q: A valid exception to "Never touch managed resources in the finalizer"? A:

I think you might be misunderstanding the question. I am not asking anyone here how to design an interface. This is not meant to be an illustration of a finished product. I am asking if my use of the finalizer is dangerous or not, given the rule I stated in the title. The example is trivial to illustrate the point only.

For the record, the property must not not return a copy of the data for the same reason that it uses ArrayPool: I am attempting to minimize the hit on the GC given how fast these frames arrive.

Q: glue_sql converts boolean into integers: How to prevent this? A:

As pointed out in the comments SQLite does not have a boolean data type although it does recognize TRUE and FALSE as synonyms for 1 and 0 so if your purpose is just to have TRUE and FALSE showing up in the SQL as TRUE and FALSE rather than 1 and 0 then we can perform preprocessing as follows:

bool <- function(x) UseMethod("bool")
bool.default <- identity
bool.logical <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) DBI::SQL("NULL") else DBI::SQL(x)

rows <- list("ABC", 1, pi, TRUE, FALSE) |> lapply(bool)
glue_sql("INSERT into table values ({rows*})", rows = rows, .con = con)
## <SQL> INSERT into table values ('ABC', 1, 3.14159265358979, TRUE, FALSE)

Q: REGEX: splitting up bank transaction statements A:

There is missing a space after the first monetary value, that can be covered by \s*:

((\d{2}) (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) (20\d{2}))(.*?)(\-[\d.,]+)? (\$[\d.,]+)?\s*(\$[\d.,]+)

Also, if there are only these tree scenarios, the regex can be adjusted to a more specific pattern:

((\d{2}) (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) (20\d{2}))\s*([a-zA-Z]+[/ ]?[a-zA-Z]*)\s*(\-[\d.,]+)?\s*(\$[\d.,]+)?\s*(\$[\d.,]+)

Q: analog to glib's object model? A:

The one I picked is Qt and is LGPL licensed. It has a class hierarchy based on QObject. It supports properties as well as a signal/slot mechanism, which allows you to get notified about changes by connecting an object's signal to either a pre-existing slot, or a slot you wrote.

The signals/slots mechanism is described here: Qt Core: Signals & Slots
